title: Assumptions Transfer — Flexible Start Pilot
description: Identify hidden premises and choose evidence that directly tests them in a workplace pilot.
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewNotes: Original transfer set for role-specific Practice/Train depth; reviewed for necessary assumptions, generalization, causation, and one-best-answer logic.

questions.prompt: Which assumption is necessary for the director's claim that every team will see the same drop in lateness?

options.text: Every employee prefers to begin work after 9:00 a.m.
options.whyWrong: The policy does not require everyone to prefer a late start.

options.text: Call volume will permanently remain low.
options.whyWrong: The director claims the same lateness reduction, not that call volume never changes.

options.text: Teams outside the pilot are similar enough to the volunteer teams for the pilot result to generalize.
Road construction can never affect commuting.
options.whyWrong: The passage explicitly identifies road conditions as a possible competing influence.

explanation.answer: Teams outside the pilot are similar enough to the volunteer teams for the pilot result to generalize.
explanation.whyCorrect: The director generalizes from two volunteer teams to every team, which requires assuming the groups are sufficiently comparable.
explanation.quickTip: A generalization depends on the tested group representing the larger group.

questions.prompt: When the director credits the policy for the entire decline in lateness, what hidden assumption is he making?

options.text: The end of nearby road construction did not meaningfully contribute to the improvement in arrival times.
Employees never arrived late before the pilot.
options.whyWrong: The passage gives a pre-pilot average of 11 late arrivals per week.

options.text: The flexible start window was exactly two hours long.
options.whyWrong: The time window is stated directly; it is not a hidden premise linking policy to outcome.

options.text: The office should eliminate all attendance rules.
options.whyWrong: Neither writer argues for eliminating attendance requirements.

explanation.answer: The end of nearby road construction did not meaningfully contribute to the improvement in arrival times.
explanation.whyCorrect: To assign the whole change to the policy, the director must discount the other simultaneous change that could affect lateness.
explanation.quickTip: Causal claims often hide an assumption that no competing cause explains the result.

questions.prompt: Which assumption underlies the director's promise that service will not be affected during office-wide adoption?

options.text: Every customer calls at the same time of day.
options.whyWrong: Service can be affected without calls arriving at exactly the same time.

options.text: Employees will stop using flexible start times after eight weeks.
options.whyWrong: The claim concerns continuing the policy, not ending it.

options.text: Supervisors volunteered because they disliked the policy.
options.whyWrong: The volunteer teams had already asked for more flexibility.

options.text: Supervisors across the office can maintain enough coverage even when more employees choose later starts.

explanation.answer: Supervisors across the office can maintain enough coverage even when more employees choose later starts.
explanation.whyCorrect: The claim about unchanged service depends on staffing coverage remaining adequate under a larger rollout.
explanation.quickTip: Ask what must be true for the promised outcome to follow from the proposal.

questions.prompt: Which new evidence would MOST directly test the assumption that the pilot result will hold during busier seasons?

options.text: A survey of whether employees like flexible schedules.
options.whyWrong: Preference does not test whether lateness and service outcomes hold under heavier call volume.

options.text: A larger flex-start trial conducted during the office’s high-volume season, with lateness and service levels tracked.
A list of the office’s busiest customer questions.
options.whyWrong: Question topics do not test whether the policy performs similarly in a busier season.

options.text: The original eight-week pilot report printed in a different format.
options.whyWrong: Reformatting the same evidence does not test the seasonal assumption.

explanation.answer: A larger flex-start trial conducted during the office’s high-volume season, with lateness and service levels tracked.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testing the policy during the condition that may differ—high call volume—directly checks whether the pilot generalizes across seasons.
explanation.quickTip: To test an assumption, gather evidence under the condition the assumption takes for granted.

curriculum.learningObjective: Identify assumptions that connect evidence to a claim and select evidence that tests those assumptions.
